column1: # RECIPE_MEMORY.tsv - append-only lesson memory of recipe planner-family-20261107 (RELOCATE_PLANNER_FAMILY): one row per lesson, appended in the same commit as the correction.

column4: an import-only closure misses types written fully qualified in a body: IndexPrecomputeSnapshot names com.synexia.job.IProgressMonitor nine times without an import; closure.py also follows qualified references, and relocate.py v4 maps them through QUALIFIED rows and refuses any qualified reference left under a mapped donor root
column5: first closure: 26 types, no job package; with qualified references: 27 (MISSING com.synexia.job.IProgressMonitor)

column4: the develop main path is not always the newest lineage: NativePrecomputeOps has a reviewed hash-pinned postimage (crate m3-tuple-fallback-scalar-java21-20261102) whose manifest before-sha256 equals the main path; the FILE row reads that postimage; for IndexPrecomputeSnapshot the hash-pinned precompute-startup postimage equals the owner-scoped-provenance preimage fixture, i.e. it is older than the main path, which stays the FILE source
column5: manifest.tsv before a0bc481fa4ff... = sha256 of the main path; postimage b716b3b6f3ed...

column4: the external progress interface pulls synexia-common progress and context-core into a donor compile (19 errors); the donor closure only calls checkCanceled() and noop(), so differential.sh generates a two-member stub from the QUALIFIED rows instead of fetching the real interface
column5: run 1: 19 javac errors in the fetched IProgressMonitor; run 2: STUB (2 members), PASS

column4: the naming rules rename the tuple root-hash domain literal, so every frozen-tuple root hash differs from the donor's; the differential compiles a second donor copy with the LITERAL rows applied (byte-identical to the relocated dump on JIT and -Xint) and compares the raw donor with the H:<sha256> fields masked (identical); the dump recomputes each root hash from the domain each side declares
column5: raw vs relocated unmasked: only the root-hash lines and TOTAL differ

column4: the donor greedy pass recurses into dependencies before marking a capability, so a cyclic dependency graph overflows the stack (StackOverflowError) once more than 20 candidates are planned; greedy catalogues of the corpus are acyclic and a CYCLE_PROBE line records the behaviour on both sides (donor bytes kept, not fixed here)

a property-only greedy reference (valid, recomputed, no positive closure still fits) let a mutant that also takes non-positive closures survive; the reference now recomputes the documented greedy pass (mandatory closures, densest positive closure with exact cross products and the planner tie-breaks) and compares the whole recommendation
javap prints a QUALIFIED type in signatures with its package; the copy maps each QUALIFIED type row (no call) to the target type in the target package before the PACKAGE and TYPE rows

a doubled backslash passed through the shell into a Python string became a backspace byte inside a regex (closure.py silently missed qualified references); recipe scripts are written by a file editor and checked for control bytes

a later hash-pinned apply recipe (planner-cycle-fix-20261107) refines one relocated target; PATCH rows let relocate.py accept that recipe's pinned after (and refuse when its pinned before is not the relocated bytes), so both recipes keep one fixed point; the anchor/PROVENANCE version stays v4 (bytes unchanged) and only the run log names v5, so no anchor line is edited
column5: relocate.py --check: FILE PATCHED M3IndexPrecomputePlanner.java, changed=0 provenance=UNCHANGED; a VERSION bump to v5 would have rewritten the anchor line of all 29 files
